note:
v1 96.751/96.765. PERIOD DOUBLING, polytempo braindance in Bohlen-Pierce tuning (13 steps to the 3:1 tritave, Lambda mode; no octaves anywhere): a clock that learns to drift.
- One number drives everything: the logistic map x <- r x (1-x), iterated each sixteenth, plays the lead on chirp's physical reed (clarinet: odd harmonics, BP's natural voice). It also decides the drum accents, ratchets and stutter chance.
- r walks the road into chaos section by section: one note (a sequencer pulse, after a damped wobble), two (7/8), four (with a rest), eight (5/4), chaos (the tempo ramping 140 -> 150), the PERIOD-THREE window (r 3.835: three sixteenths running across the 4/4), the storm (r 4, 11/8 at 154), then settling back to one note as it slows to 132.
- Polytempo: blips on a 5:4 grid from the map's twin, a folded-sine bass on a 3:4 grid. BP 3:5:7 chords on a glass pad. Meter changes and tempo ramps live in the tempo map.
Spectrum: v1 at first was 10-19 dB heavy at 70-640 Hz and 10-17 dB dull above 4 kHz (folded bass, 909 body); the bass came down 9 dB, the kick 4 dB with an hp, and a ride and louder hats came in: spectrum 20 -> 92, cohesion 12 -> 100. Flow 46: t8's tail differs (+28 dB at 300-600 Hz on my side); a ticking intro to meet it cost variety, so it was dropped. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
